summary: Retested the two iteration-172 fixes and tested end to end the destination-first imports that had not been tested before. Everything ran in a disposable isolated DB (iso_harness_book170: Motor handles patched, structure.seed() called, storage and AI mocked, the real sandboxed PDF and Excel organiser workers used). New suite tests/structure_imports_iso174.py: 46 of 51 checks pass. Both fixes hold. (a) A mock scheduled with its own release_at shows 'scheduled' with counts.scheduled=1 while another mock is published now, and it switches to 'published' once its own release_at passes. The book-level release_at stays null. In the UI, book-progress-counts shows '1 SCHEDULED'. (b) The 'publish' control action returns auto_publish=False, in both the response and the DB. Paper PDF import into bitsat:mocks works: the destination is stored, the paper reads as BITSAT, and after scheduling the set has catalog_section_id='bitsat:mocks' with a catalog_order after the existing tests and is listed in the admin section tests. A paper that reads as JEE Main returns 409 when uploaded to BITSAT, with a clear message, and no set is created. A custom-exam destination sets exam to the custom exam key (catalog_order 1, then 2). Excel (combined template filled with 3 TEST rows) behaves the same: the destination is stored, the set is placed after the PDF set, the mismatch returns 409 and the custom exam key is used. Chapter books: list, pyq and unknown sections are rejected 422. Missing request_id, a non-PDF name and reviewer access are rejected. The destination is stored for bitsat:chapters. A junk PDF fails cleanly. Using a scripted organiser result for process_book only, a JEE result uploaded to bitsat:chapters fails with the 'reads as JEE Main' message and creates no sets. A BITSAT result places the chapter sets in bitsat:chapters as drafts that are not live. A custom chapters section gives exam = the custom key. Frontend via bridge173: the wizard paper and excel forms upload, then show wizard-done, wizard-existing-list (TEST_BM1, TEST_BM2), wizard-new-item (Queued) and wizard-open-review linking to /studio/imports/{id}. The review page shows the paper as BITSAT, 3 questions, Ready. Checked on desktop 1920x800 and on mobile 390x844 (excel). The chapter form appears for bitsat:chapters. A chapter type on a list section falls back to the type step. Exams & Content shows '1 test' / '0 tests'. The bridge DB was dropped and no isolated DB is left. No customer-DB writes: 0 TEST_ docs found there.

minor.issue: A mock scheduled with its own release_at, then paused, then resumed, is shown as 'published' even though its release_at and set start_at are still in the future. book_imports.py:251 uses only book.payload.release_at and ignores mock.release_at. The label and counts are wrong. Students are not exposed because the set start_at is still in the future.

A PDF paper import accepts a chapters-layout section_id (bitsat:chapters or a custom chapters section) with 202, because imports.py calls destination() with the default layouts ('list','chapters'). The wizard only offers paper for list sections, so only the API allows this. Excel in chapters sections is intended (TYPES.excel.layouts), so pass ('list',) when format=='pdf'.

An extra form field returns 400 (Starlette max_fields error) instead of the 422 that imports return. Also, re-uploading the same PDF with a different or invalid section_id returns the old book before destination() validates the new section, so the new destination is silently ignored.
An empty file part returns 413 'Use PDF files within the displayed size limit' (imports.py:109 `not raw`). This is misleading; it should be 422 'file is empty'.
ImportView shows exam='JEE Main' (the detected exam) for an import scheduled into a custom exam, whose set exam is the custom key. ImportView also does not expose the destination.

issues: The schedule form uses the browser's native date and time inputs (mm/dd/yyyy) instead of the shadcn calendar used elsewhere
The page header says 'PDF IMPORT · CUSTOM PRACTICE' and does not show where the test will go (BITSAT › Mock Tests), so the destination-first context is lost after the wizard

action_items: book_imports.py resume_mock: compute state = 'scheduled' if (mock.release_at or book.payload.release_at or 0) > stamp, or use the set start_at
imports.py create_import: use destination(section_id, ('list',)) when format=='pdf' (keep ('list','chapters') for xlsx)
chapter_books.upload_book: validate section_id before the `old` dedupe return; return 422 for extra form fields
imports.py: return 422 for an empty uploaded file instead of 413
Optional: expose the destination and the effective exam in ImportView, and show the destination chip on the import review page; use the shadcn date picker in the import schedule form
critical_code_review_comments: resume_mock ignores the per-mock release_at (same class of bug as the iteration-172 book_view fix)
The layout check for create_import is format-agnostic, unlike books (list only) and chapter books (chapters only)
chapter upload: the receipt and dedupe run before destination validation, so a changed destination is not applied to an existing book

success_rate.backend: 90% (46/51 new checks; the 5 failures are the minor issues above)

seed_data_creation: Only inside disposable isolated DBs (tejas_isolated_book170_*), all dropped. Nothing was written to the customer DB.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend: cd /app/backend && python tests/structure_imports_iso174.py (about 40s, 51 checks). The failing check names map to the minor issues: 'pdf import section chapters layout 422', 'pdf import section custom chapters 422', 'xlsx chapters section 422' (this one is intended behaviour, so change the test to expect 202), 'chapter book extra field 422', 'resume_mock keeps per-mock scheduled state'. The chapter organiser is monkeypatched (chapter_books.organise_pdfs) only for the process_book destination paths, because no combined TEJAS200 chapter fixture exists. Browser: start nohup timeout 2400 python tests/structure_bridge173.py 2300 > /tmp/bridge173.log &, then run python tests/ui_fixtures174.py. IMPORTANT: Playwright route interception drops multipart file bodies (the bridge received 700 bytes and returned 413). Add an init script that wraps window.fetch and converts a FormData body to an ArrayBuffer via new Response(fd).arrayBuffer(), copying its content-type, before route.fetch to http://127.0.0.1:8773. Stop the bridge with pkill -INT so it drops its DB.
rca of the issue: Wizard 413 during the first UI run: a harness artifact, not an app bug. Chromium request interception does not carry File blobs in multipart postData, so the bridge received empty file parts and imports.py:109 returned 413 for the empty file. Fixed in the test by serialising the FormData in the page. resume_mock: book_imports.py:251 checks only the book-level release_at, so a per-mock schedule is reported as published after a resume.
